q3Options.text: It succeeds without error while discarding whatever content came after the cut point
It raises a visible exception every time content is too long
q3Options.reason: That's the opposite of what makes it dangerous, if it raised a visible exception, it would be a loud, easy-to-catch bug, not a silent one.

q3Options.text: It only affects performance, not correctness
q3Options.reason: It affects correctness directly, whatever content was cut off is simply unavailable to the model, that's a correctness problem, not a performance one.

q4Options.text: More total tokens processed across the whole document, since boundary content is repeated, which raises cost and total latency
Nothing, overlap is free since it reuses content that was already fetched
q4Options.reason: 'Already fetched' doesn't mean free to process, the model still has to read those repeated tokens again in the next chunk, that's real additional token cost, not a free reuse.

q4Options.text: It reduces the number of chunks needed
q4Options.reason: Overlap doesn't reduce chunk count, if anything, more overlap per chunk boundary means slightly MORE total chunks are needed to cover the same content, not fewer.

q5Options.text: Roughly 950 tokens total (600 + 150 + 200), noticeably more than a single successful ~800-token call (600 prompt + 200 response)
The same as a single call, retries don't add token cost, only latency
q5Options.reason: Retries absolutely add token cost, the original prompt is sent again (plus new error context), and a new response is generated, that's real additional tokens billed, not just extra wait time.

q5Options.text: Less than a single call, since the second attempt is shorter
q5Options.reason: The second attempt isn't a replacement for the first, both attempts' tokens count, the original 600-token prompt was already sent (and paid for) on the first, failed attempt.
